reason: Holds for many components, but LargeLoader is exported only as a named `export const`, so the blanket default-export convention overreaches.
Reusing mx_IconizedContextMenu_option_red gives base red color only; task explicitly requires new destructive CSS and hover/focus states, and the rule is scoped to IconizedContextMenu.
toSqlArgs snake-cases JSON tag keys, not field names: NewPassword emits `password`, Password (`json:"-"`) is dropped; no `new_password` key exists.
'Regardless' wrongly covers enabled-legacy plus shorthand, which must be rejected; but the agent's code rejects that case first, so the refutation is weak.
At baseline no smart-rule evaluation writes playlist_tracks; GetWithTracks only loads existing rows, so smart playlists don't persist evaluated tracks.
Configured() is true for any nonempty EnabledFlag (true, on, 1), so 'only yes or no' omits values; agent likely meant 'set at all'.
The proposed catch calls setError, and InitContainer throws whenever error is set, so non-404 migration failures still block Drive from loading.
userFilter applies the public-or-owner predicate only to non-admins; admins get an empty And, so admin non-owners can read private playlists.
An empty cid array hits an early `return []` before helpers.isAllowedTo, so helpers are called only for non-empty arrays.
Per Qt docs and the AppArmor profile, qtwebengine_locales lives inside the translations directory, not beside it.
Normalizing the name isn't strictly necessary, but the verifier's alternative still requests INTERPRETER_PYTHON, effectively the same python key, so refutation is weak.
Gomega Equal is type-strict (reflect.DeepEqual); the untyped constant defaults to int, so an int32 actual would fail.
readyRead fires only for the current stdout channel; without connecting readyReadStandardError, stderr-only output never triggers _on_ready_read.
_ansiballz_main runs on the managed node and writes its zip payload itself; the controller's temp-file transfer is elsewhere and skipped under pipelining.
Base assigns cover_url only after author lookup succeeds and overwrites provided values, so the listed requirement needs new behavior, not existing behavior.
Some duration fields allow int, but audit.buffer.flush_period is string-only in the CUE schema, so not every numeric duration matches.
cvedict.Fortinet exposes Cwes, PublishedDate, LastModifiedDate; the code uses nonexistent fields CweIDs, Published, LastModified, so it won't compile.
hasVPN matches only PLANS.VPN, missing legacy VPNBASIC/VPNPLUS; but requirements never mention legacy plans and the claim is a hedged guess.
version_check defaults to compiled=True, checking runtime, compiled Qt and PyQt; '< 6.7.0' holds for runtime only when all versions agree.
Languages are Infogami Things; name_translated is an embedded Thing without values(), which resolves to nothing, so translated names are silently skipped.
A fresh struct zeroes ExpiresAt, so description-only updates clear expiration; but creating and updating is feasible and type-compatible, so refutation is strict.
Storage is JSON-like, but Infogami's _process converts every dict, including nested TOC authors, into keyless Thing objects on read.
Qt 6.9 docs still list ForceDarkMode, and BASE's >=6.3 variant keeps dark-mode setting names, so nothing was removed.
The existing auth interceptor already puts Authentication in context; audit middleware can read the OIDC email via GetAuthenticationFrom without modifying it.
The guest test passes one request.jar to both the topic POST and the reply, so both share a session ID.
canReply throws topic-deleted only when the author isn't admin/mod; a queued post by a category moderator into a deleted topic succeeds.
The requirement explicitly limits team checks to orgs with configured team restrictions, so fallback is mentioned and a global team block is wrong.
toModels must preserve PostScan-normalized values; applying normalization there recomputes (e.g., normalized 2 becomes 1), contradicting the no-recompute requirement.
The timestamp-plus-size layout fits only default timestamp-based pycs; Python 3.8 hash-based pycs store a source hash in those bytes.
Trivy v0.30.0 defines TypeLicenseFile, not analyzer.TypeLicense, so the proposed append references a nonexistent identifier and won't compile.
No testenv.New exists at baseline; but the agent knowingly reconstructed it and the requirement mandates bufconn plus gRPC server, so refutation is weak.
The issue also names respawn.py, compat/selinux.py, executor/module_common.py and package modules like apt.py, dnf.py, yum.py.
newSelectWithAnnotation uses the receiver's tableName; called on playlistRepository it joins item_type='playlist', not 'media_file', so annotations mismatch.
The old config set includes TOML/HCL types absent from Trivy 0.30 and lacks Helm; it's the legacy list, not the target API's.
Besides output views, the issue mandates endpoint fields, wildcard expansion, TCP probing, parsing rules and in-place status updates.
The authors/infobox template renders only an illustration, Wikidata description and date table; no links-with-logos section exists.
Only 'Chapter missing pipe' is in the test module; the other three are docstring `>>>` examples, though those are arguably doctests.
Kube embeds Service, which already exports Configured(); redefining Configured() on Kube shadows it without adding a new public method.
functools.lru_cache doesn't exist in Python 2.7, which this module_utils code must support, so the decorated method fails to define there.
The debug branch checks only the setting, not event type, so non-debug events get logged instead of ignored as the contract requires.
